newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech still sees long distance in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech still sees long distance in Q1.

text.p: Ameritech Corp, one of the regional Bell telephone companies, said Friday its plans to enter the long-distance telephone market in the first quarter of 1997 remained in place.
"It is still our plan to be in long distance in first quarter 1997," Richard Notebaert, chairman and chief executive of Ameritech said in an interview.

Still, the company had to be flexible, Notebaert cautioned. The entry of regional telecommunications companies into the U.S. long-distance market from their operating areas is dependent on the opening of the local telephone monopolies.

Other regional phone companies -- but not Ameritech -- have asked the Eighth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to uphold a temporary freeze on the Federal Communication Commission's rules, which were due to take effect last Monday.

At issue is the price other carriers would pay for access to the Baby Bells' local lines. The FCC rules require they give a 17 to 25 percent discount from retail prices, but some say the FCC lacked the authority to impose pricing rules on state regulators overseeing negotiations among the operators.
"We think there should be expedited handling of the case to get it fixed rather than just say everything stops. Customers don't stop," Notebaert said.
Ameritech has, however, asked that the pricing formula in the FCC's orders be overturned.
"We kind of like the 10 to 13 percent range," he said, adding the current range "is not fun, but it's liveable."
Even if the freeze is upheld, Notebaert said it would not necessarily keep Ameritech from entering the long-distance market.
"If it's a stay only on state's rights versus federal, I don't see any reason why we couldn't proceed," he said.
